extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners drafting European patent applications (especially in chemistry/pharmaceuticals) and advising on EPO prosecution
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting and prosecuting European patent claims that define compositions or processes by numeric or characteristic parameters, with attention to EPO clarity (Art.84) and sufficiency (Art.83) requirements and Board of Appeal case law. Focused on when to include measurement methods, how to handle open-ended ranges, and how to preserve amendment basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of parameters (EPO Guidelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parameters are characteristic values, which may be values of directly measurable properties (e.g. the melting point of a substance, the flexural strength of a steel, the resistance of an electrical conductor). The characteristics of a product may be specified by parameters related to the physical structure of the product, provided that those parameters can be clearly and reliably determined by objective procedures which are usual in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this EPO definition to determine whether a feature in your claim is a 'parameter' and therefore subject to the Guidelines' requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameters must be clearly and reliably determinable by objective procedures usual in the art
rubrics_metrics.description: A critical requirement from the Guidelines is that the parameter 'can be clearly and reliably determined by objective procedures which are usual in the art'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When drafting parameter-based claims, ensure the parameter can be measured by objective, well-established procedures in the relevant technical field; otherwise the EPO may object.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity — claims must be clear in themselves (Art.84(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: For Article 84 EPC clarity, each parameter needs to meet the requirement that the claims must be clear in themselves when read by the skilled person (not including knowledge derived from the description).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on the description to supply essential measurement details needed to make the claim intelligible to the skilled person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity — measurement method must appear in the claim (Art.84(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The method for measuring a parameter (or at least a reference thereto) must appear completely in the claim itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferably include the measurement method wording directly in the claim; alternatively, have an explicit reference or text in the description that can be incorporated into the claim during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity — verifiability by the skilled person (Art.84(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who chooses to define the scope of the claim by parameters needs to ensure that the skilled person can easily and unambiguously verify whether they are working inside or outside the scope of the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft parameter thresholds and measurement instructions so that a practitioner can reproducibly test whether a product or process falls within the claimed scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — measurement method may be omitted if common general knowledge applies
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement that the measurement method appear in the claim may be met if the measurement method to be employed belongs to the skilled person's common general knowledge, e.g. because there is only one method, or because a particular method is commonly used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there truly is a single, universally used method in the art, omission of the method in the claim may be acceptable; but be cautious and document common practice in the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — omission acceptable if all methods yield same result within accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement may also be met if all the measurement methodologies known in the relevant technical field for determining this parameter yield the same result within the appropriate limit of measurement accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider providing evidence or argument that alternative measurement methods produce equivalent results to support omission of a specific method from the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution on open-ended ranges (Article 83 — sufficiency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open-ended ranges (e.g. 'at least X') can, in certain circumstances, fail Article 83 EPC (sufficiency) because such ranges may include embodiments not obtainable using the invention disclosed in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although Board decision T 0398/19 indicates that open-ended ranges alone are not necessarily insufficient, prefer to disclose reasonable upper limits in the description so they can be added to claims if required; ensure ranges are expressed so as to meet EPO requirements for the basis of amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical drafting advice to preserve amendment basis
rubrics_metrics.description: If the claim does not itself include the measurement method, ensure the description includes text that describes the method for measuring the parameter(s) and which can easily be added to the claim during prosecution. Preferably have some text in the description that can be added verbatim to the claims to meet the EPO's strict requirements regarding the basis for any amendments that are made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft description passages with clear, copy-able measurement protocols and reasonable limits (e.g. upper bounds for open-ended ranges) so you can amend claims later without running afoul of the EPO's amendment-basis rules.
